findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/research/scope.md §2.3 (first bullet), §2.6, §3.2 'Sources of the prayer', §3.8 and §3.10 'Sources', §5.1 (first bullet); src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/research/source-bindings.toml, binding artifact.catholic-church.sacramentarium-gelasianum-vetus.wilson-1894.ia-djvu-ocr-gelasiansacrame00wilsgoog (context)
findings.problem: The research records that literal searches of the registered Wilson 1894 Gelasian optical layer (SHA-256 039123ca..., which it says it re-fetched and matched) for 'contagia', 'pura mente', 'Sanctificationibus' and 'suppliciter deprecamur ut haec' returned none of the three orations, and §5.1 lists them as 'searched and not found' in the Old Gelasian. That exact file (re-fetched by this review, same digest) contains the Collect at physical line 21522 ('Da, quaesumus, Domine, populo tuo diabolica vitare ... contagia, et te solum Dominum puro corde sectari', Liber III, Missa XIII, Wilson p. 231; apparatus: S3 Gerb. 'Deum', Pam. 'pura mente') and the Secret at line 21533 ('Maiestatem tuam, Domine, suppliciter deprecamur, ut haec sancta ...', same Missa, whose Postcommunion is a different prayer, 'Praesta ... divino munere satiati', p. 232). Lines 30119-30123 (Wilson's appendix, p. 359) list all three orations, the Postcommunion 'Sanctificationibus tuis' included, under 'Hebd. xxi post Pentecosten' in Gerbert's Frankish Gelasian, and Wilson's note to Missa XIII says R., S. and Gerb. assign its Collect and Secret to the twenty-first Sunday after Pentecost. The same text stands in the other registered Wilson 1894 layer (LiberSacramentorumRomanaeEcclesiae_djvu.txt, 25586b16...). The claimed negative search is therefore false. The transmission history in §2.6 omits the oldest witness, the Collect's textual history (Dominum/Deum, puro corde/pura mente) is incomplete, and a study drafted from this record would state that the orations are absent from the Gelasian tradition.
findings.required_result: Correct §§2.3, 2.6, 3.2, 3.8, 3.10 and 5.1 and the Wilson 1894 binding context. Record the Old Gelasian witness of the Collect and Secret at Liber III, Missa XIII (Wilson 1894 pp. 231-232), with its apparatus variants and its different Postcommunion. Record the Frankish Gelasian placement of all three orations at Hebd. XXI post Pentecosten (Wilson's appendix p. 359, and the R./S./Gerb. note). Check these readings on page images or state that only the optical layer was read. Revise the evidentiary consequence, and the Collect's echo notes on puro corde/pura mente and Dominum/Deum, in the light of this evidence. Re-run every other literal-search negative recorded over an optical layer with a method that tolerates line breaks, marginal sigla and punctuation, and correct any other false negative it finds.

CXXXVI')
findings.problem: The orations and the O antiphonary cues this record uses stand in the Supplement that Wilson prints after the 'Hucusque' preface (p. 145 onward). Wilson's own introduction says the second part 'is a supplement to the Gregorian Liber Sacramentorum arranged by a person not named', and the Supplement's table of chapters lists the Sundays after Pentecost. They do not stand in the Hadrianum. The section numbers are XXXIIII, XXXV and XXXVI: the tracked leaf n231 (p. 174) prints 'a/XXXIIII. DOMINICA .XVI.' and 'bXXXV. DOMINICA .XVII.', and the p. 175 optical layer reads 'XXXVI. DOMINICA .XVIII.', with superscript footnote letters, not a 'C', before each number. The record nonetheless calls the Sunday count 'the Hadrianum's' and cites 'sect. CXXXVI' in five places and in the binding. A study drafted from it would attribute to the papal Hadrianum orations that the Hadrianum does not contain, and would cite a locus that does not exist.
findings.required_result: Identify the witness throughout as the Supplement to the Gregorian Sacramentary in Wilson's edition. Correct every locus to Supplement sect. XXXVI, p. 175, and the cue footnotes to sects. XXXIIII-XXXVI, pp. 174-175. Remove the 'Hadrianum's count' wording. Restate the orations' transmission sequence together with the RES-001 Gelasian evidence: Old Gelasian Sunday series, Frankish Gelasian Hebd. XXI, Supplement Dominica XVIII, 1962 Seventeenth Sunday.

findings.problem: Two of the three anagogical clauses rest on words this Mass does not appoint. 'the servant asks to be taught God's justifications' is Ps 118:124b ('et iustificationes tuas doce me'), which the Introit does not sing (propers/verified.md §1, 'Construction'). 'until the justice that is everlasting (Dan 9:24) is brought in' comes from Dan 9:24, outside the Offertory's 9:17-19; scope §1.2 records that the seventy weeks are not appointed and that later prose must mark them. Neither clause is marked as unsung context, and no checked witness is given for the anagogical link. Jerome on 9:24 sets out the computations of the seventy weeks and declines to judge between them (scope §4.7); he is not cited for this sense. This breaks the contract's rule that each interpretation's spiritual senses stay anchored in the literal text and checked reception, and it invites the study to put an unsung petition in the Introit's mouth.
findings.required_result: Rewrite the anagogical sense of just-judge-merciful-hearer from appointed words and checked reception. Suitable anchors are the Introit's 'secundum misericordiam tuam' with Augustine s. 26.5, the Postcommunion's 'remedia aeterna', and the Communion's 'terribili apud omnes reges terrae' with Augustine En. in Ps. 75, 18 or Rupert and Durandus. If Ps 118:124b or Dan 9:24 is kept, mark it explicitly as unsung context reached through a named witness at an exact locus, and mark the connection [E].

findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/research/interpretations.md §2.3 (son-and-lord-of-david), `secret` row; src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/propers/verified.md 'Discrepancies between the two 1962 witnesses' (Secret, conclusion row: 'The typical edition prints this one conclusion in full') and §8 'Conclusion'
findings.problem: Reading 2's only stated contribution from the Secret is 'Its long conclusion, the only one printed in full in this formulary ... the prayer's own confession of the Son reigning with the Father in unity'. The conclusion is not printed in full. It stops at 'in unitate', whereas Rubricae generales n. 115 a (facsimile PDF p. 17) gives the full form, continuing 'Spiritus Sancti, Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen'. The printed length is a typographic variable, not a property of this prayer. The typica prints the same long form at many orations: its text layer has about 300 occurrences of '...regnat in unitate', including the Fifteenth Sunday's Secret, no. 1589, and its Postcommunion, both on PDF p. 478. It prints 'Per Dominum' at others, including the Sixteenth Sunday's Secret. The Benziger printing conformed to the typica gives this Secret as 'Per Dominum.'. Under RG 115 a, the Collect, Secret and Postcommunion of this Mass all conclude identically when said. The contribution therefore rests on typography, and it would lead the study to present a feature shared by all three orations as distinctive of this Secret.
findings.required_result: Correct verified.md to say that the Secret's conclusion is printed at length only as far as 'in unitate', and that the printed length of a conclusion is a typographic variable while RG 115 governs the conclusion in use. Replace the Secret row of son-and-lord-of-david with a contribution grounded in the Secret's own words or in checked reception. If that is not possible, record honestly that its contribution to this reading is minimal and shared with the other orations. Imply no distinctiveness either way.

findings.problem: The chronology corpus already has a traditional-attribution relation (src/sources/chronology/bindings.yaml, first binding, subject israel.monarchy.david-traditional-era). It binds psalms whose tracked Douay or Clementine titles name David. Ps 32 qualifies (Douay Ps 32:1 'A psalm for David.'; Clementine 'Psalmus David.') but is outside that binding's scope. The concise page-2 Gradual cell will therefore carry only the critical 'Before c. 165 B.C.' boundary, although the 1962 profile asks for the traditional attribution to lead where the received chronology supplies it. The research recorded the gap for the chronology owner but routed it nowhere specific. Its wording ('the dossier may not supply one') could also be read as forbidding the textual observation that the titles name David (Ps 32) and Asaph (Ps 75).
findings.required_result: Ask the chronology corpus owner to extend the Davidic traditional-attribution binding to Ps 32, citing bible:douay-rheims:Ps.32.1 and the Clementine title, then regenerate research/chronology.toml and chronology-annotations.tex. Otherwise, record in scope.md why this is not done. Clarify in §7.4 that the page-2 explanatory row may state the Vulgate/Douay titles as textual observations without attaching any date.

findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/research/scope.md §2 (esp. §2.6) and §3.3 'Literary context'; src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/research/interpretations.md §4.2, row 'Oldest stable layer it rests on'
findings.problem: The Epistle belongs to the semi-continuous Pauline course of the Sundays after Pentecost. The facsimile prints Eph 3:13-21 for the Sixteenth Sunday (PDF p. 478), Eph 4:1-6 for this Sunday, and 1 Cor 1:4-8 for the Eighteenth (PDF p. 491), and Ephesians resumes on later Sundays. verified.md notes the Missal's dropping of 'itaque', which points back to chapter 3, the text the previous Sunday reads. Rupert, Durandus and Guéranger show that this Epistle stayed in place while the Gospel moved. The record never documents this course, which is the most direct Ordinary-Time evidence that the Epistle was not chosen to match the Gospel. The §4.2 row gives 'the 1962 Gospel and Epistle' as the oldest stable layer for readings 1 and 2, setting the least stable element, the Gospel (scope §2.4), beside the stable Epistle.
findings.required_result: Record the Epistle's place in the Pauline course with facsimile loci, and add it to §2.6's evidentiary consequence. Revise the §4.2 row so that it separates the long-stable Epistle from the later-placed Gospel.

findings.location: src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/research/scope.md §3.1, §3.5, §3.7, §3.9 (Greek, medieval and later, and negative-results rows) and §5.2
findings.problem: No Greek exegesis was sampled for the Introit, Alleluia, Communion or Offertory. Theodoret's Interpretatio in Psalmos is registered and was not opened, and no Greek reading of Daniel 9 was sought through a public delivery, although other public deliveries were used elsewhere. No medieval Doctor or later canonized psalm commentator was sought for Pss 32, 75, 101 or 118; St Robert Bellarmine's Explanatio in Psalmos, which has a public-domain English translation, is one example. §5.2 does not name that family as unreached. The Communion row's 'Aquinas's Postilla super Psalmos not consulted' implies the Postilla covers Ps 75, but it ends at Ps 54. The sweep is honestly bounded and still supports three readings, so this does not block drafting.
findings.required_result: Either open Theodoret at Pss 32, 75, 101 and 118 and search one later canonized psalm commentator for the four psalms, adding any retained witness to the matrix, or name these families explicitly as unreached in §5.2. Correct the Postilla statements to reflect its range.

summary: Cold review of the research records of the Claude 1962 leaf 57-seventeenth-after-pentecost (context, scope, interpretations, verified/retrieved propers, source bindings, review dependencies, chronology record and annotations). Occurrence, identity, rank, rubrics, the ten-element inventory and its boundaries were confirmed on the hash-matched CMAA facsimile page images (PDF 479-481 and the rubric, Calendarium and Beata gens loci). The 1862 antecedent leaves, the gregorien.info view (digest matched), the Wilson 1915 leaf and layer, the Wilson 1894 layers, the chronology labels (current Catholic Encyclopedia deliveries) and the chronology record and annotation currency were also checked, and source-library validation passed. The retained patristic and medieval loci checked this stage were Jerome on Matthew and Ephesians (PL 26 images, digest matched) and on Daniel; Augustine En. in Ps. 32, 75, 101, 109 and 118, De doctrina christiana and De pecc. mer.; Cassiodorus on Pss 32, 75, 101 and 118; Chrysostom on Matthew and Ephesians; Gregory hom. 38; Aquinas on Matthew and Ephesians; Irenaeus; Rupert; Durandus; Guéranger; and Schuster. Nearly all read as recorded. Four blocking defects remain, all research-owned. The claimed negative search of the Old Gelasian is false: the registered layer contains the Collect and Secret, and Gerbert's Frankish Gelasian contains all three orations. Wilson 1915's Supplement is misidentified as the Hadrianum, with non-existent section numbers. The anagogical sense of reading 3 rests on unsung text. Reading 2's Secret contribution rests on typography. Three advisories cover the Ps 32 Davidic-attribution corpus gap, the undocumented semi-continuous Epistle course, and unsampled Greek and later saintly psalm exegesis. Not re-read by this review: Basil De Spiritu Sancto 16.38, Augustine De moribus I.11.18, the Trent decree, Swete's Daniel and the two dated Ordos. Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED.
